name: Methow River (Winthrop – Twisp)
blurb: Western-town float from Winthrop's Red Barn — tubers in late summer, quick spring water.

sections.notes: Late-summer float from Mack Lloyd Park/Red Barn to the Big Eddy/Rising Eagle roadside turnout. Big Eddy has a steep unimproved carry, no boat ramp, and can be difficult for larger boats; scout the actual landing and carry before setting a shuttle. Respect posted parking restrictions and private land. AW rates the full 50-mile guide reach II(III); that is not a certification of current conditions on this shorter float.
sections.routeReview: Approximate river-course overview only. The generalized historical line can cross exposed gravel bars; it does not map safe bridge passages or shoreline carries. Identify the usable landing and current hazards before launching.

putInAccess.sourceName: Town of Winthrop — Mack Lloyd Park water-access progress report, accepted by Washington RCO December 18, 2024
putInAccess.note: The accepted December 2024 project report documents the water-access ramp, bank stabilization and parking as complete, with restroom work and signage still planned. Its dated project photographs show the concrete-plank access ramp. The current RCO project remains administratively active; that status and the unfinished restroom work are not evidence that the ramp was never built. The July 2026 attachment labelled As Built contains October 2023 bid drawings and is not used as completion evidence. The RCO worksite coordinate is retained only as an approximate facility location. No exact landing, verified bank, seasonal availability or navigation-safe channel is claimed.
putInAccess.directions: Use the public Mack Lloyd Park access area behind the Winthrop Barn at 51 N Highway 20. Follow the designated river-access path. This marker identifies the project/facility area, not the precise shoreline ramp; check posted conditions and Town notices before a trip.

takeOutAccess.operator: Washington State Department of Transportation roadside turnout (per Yakama Nation-commissioned assessment)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Yakama Nation-commissioned Middle Methow recreational-use assessment — Rising Eagle Road turnout; American Whitewater Methow access guide
takeOutAccess.note: The Yakama Nation-commissioned assessment (printed page 8 and Figure 3 on page 9) identifies the WSDOT Rising Eagle turnout as an intermediate boating put-in/take-out about four river miles below Winthrop. American Whitewater independently identifies Big Eddy at SR 20 mile 196.7, describes its steep carry and supplies this coordinate. The coordinate, Rising Eagle Road/SR 20 road identity and turnout are consistent on the saved road context and individual imagery. The historical public-access assessment and current guide establish an approximate access facility, not a surveyed landing or an assurance of present conditions. No bank, safe exit, larger-boat ramp or public ownership beyond the documented access is claimed.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use only permitted parking at the large SR 20 turnout near mile 196.7 and Rising Eagle Road. This is unimproved roadside access with a steep carry between the road and river, not a boat ramp. Scout the bank, usable landing, carry and posted restrictions before launching; it can be difficult for larger boats. Do not use private driveways or assume adjoining shoreline is public.

sections.notes: Big Eddy/Rising Eagle is unimproved roadside access with a steep carry, not a boat ramp. Twisp Park has public river access but no established larger-watercraft put-in ramp in the Town plan. The confluence landing and steep carry can be difficult, especially at high water; scout the exit and suitability for your craft before launching. Area markers do not identify exact bank connections.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Town of Twisp 2022 Parks and Recreation Plan — park inventory and river access points; Yakama Nation-commissioned Middle Methow recreational-use assessment
takeOutAccess.note: The Town park plan documents the park, riparian/beach land and existing official river access. The Yakama Nation-commissioned 2011 assessment explicitly identifies Twisp Park as a public-lands access and take-out (printed page 8). RCO project 02-1329 identifies Town ownership and the park worksite coordinate, which falls within the playground/pool area in imagery. The old recreation-grant coordinate is not a ramp survey, and the grant was for park amenities, not a river landing. No bank, exact shoreline connection, new boat ramp, navigation safety or current seasonal availability is inferred.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use Twisp Park at the north end of Lincoln Street beside the Wagner Pool and Twisp/Methow confluence. This is an approximate public park/access area, not a shoreline landing or improved raft ramp. The Town plan identifies existing river access but no larger-watercraft put-in; confirm the landing, carry and suitability for your craft before floating.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

mapAuditNote: Rechecked November 17, 2026. Mack Lloyd/Red Barn and Twisp Park have Town/RCO facility support. Big Eddy corresponds to the Rising Eagle highway turnout documented in the Yakama Nation-commissioned river-use assessment and AW guide. All markers are approximate facility/roadside areas, not precise shore landings. Big Eddy requires a steep unimproved carry; current signs and bank/river conditions must be checked. No live calibration or GPS timing is approved.
